newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian refining capacity seen exceeding demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian refining capacity seen exceeding demand.

text.p: India's refining capacity is expected to reach 131 million tonnes by the year 2001-02 against a projected demand of 113 million tonnes, the independent Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) said.
A CMIE survey found that eight refinery projects were under implementation while 11 others were under various stages of planning or seeking approvals.

"These 19 projects envisaged an aggregated refining capacity of 104 million tonnes. Assuming all these projects materialise, the total refining capacity by the end of 2002 would stand at 164 million tonnes," the report said.
CMIE said according to its information, until September 1996, only five new refineries and three expansion projects were under various stages of implementation.

These eight projects would add 46 to 47 million tonnes of refining capacity by 1999-2000. The yearwise addition to capacity from these eight refineries would be (in million tonnes) 2.0 in 1996/97, 9.0 in 1997/98, 33 in 1998/99 and 3.0 in 1999/2000.

During 1996/97, capacity expansion of Bongaigaon Refinery and the Haldia refinery of Indian Oil Corp were scheduled for completion, CMIE said. Bongaigaon has completed expansion and the Haldia expansion is expected to go on stream in December 1996.

Fiscal 1997/98 would see Indian Oil adding nine million tonnes to its refining capacity. Its six million tonnes Panipat refinery is scheduled for commissioning by August 1997 and completion of a three million tonne expansion at its Koyali refinery is expected by December 1997.

More than 70 percent of the likely 46 million tonnes capacity addition is expected to come up in 1998/99. During the year, refineries of Reliance Petroleum, Essar Oil, Bharat Oman and expansion of Hindustan Petroleum Corporation are scheduled for commission.
These four projects have a combined capacity of 33 million tonnes. The three million tonn Numaligarh refinery is also expected to be commissioned by 1999/2000.
